evals.name: double-charge
evals.prompt: Can you check the new Pro checkout for what could break before we launch?
evals.expected_output: Reports that a double tap or a network retry charges the student twice, because neither the button nor the charge call uses a request key, citing pay-submit.ts. Ranks it first for harm (money). Also notes the charge has no error handling for a declined card.
assertions: The same payment taken twice (idempotency) is among the top three findings, citing pay-submit.ts with a line number.
It names the test: send the same request twice and expect one charge.
It notes what happens when the charge fails or is declined.
No file is edited.

evals.name: upload-halfway-and-size
evals.prompt: what are the edge cases in the recording upload?
evals.expected_output: Finds no size limit on the recording, no handling when the app closes or the network drops mid-upload, and an orphan file when the second call fails after the first succeeds.
assertions: It reports an unbounded file size as a finding because nothing sets a limit.
It reports the upload stopping halfway and names what is left behind, such as a file in storage with no record.
It mentions offline or slow network on the phone.
Each finding cites upload-recording.ts.

evals.name: empty-list
evals.prompt: Review RecordingsList before I ship it
evals.expected_output: Finds that a new student with no recordings crashes the screen, because recordings[0] is read without a guard.
assertions: The first finding is the empty list (nothing there), citing the recordings[0] line.
It says what the student sees: a crash or a blank screen.
It names the test: render with an empty list.

evals.name: error-path-model-call
evals.prompt: /edge-cases summarise.ts
evals.expected_output: Finds no timeout or error handling on the model call, and JSON.parse of the reply with no check, so a slow provider or a reply in another shape breaks the summary.
assertions: It reports the missing timeout and error handling on the model call (error handling).
It reports JSON.parse on an unchecked model reply (wrong kind of input).
It names a test that drives a failed or malformed reply.

evals.name: other-users-note
evals.prompt: check notes-route.ts for edge cases
evals.expected_output: Finds that any signed-in user can read another user's note by changing the id, because the query does not check the owner. Ranks it high for privacy.
assertions: The top finding is reading another user's note (authorisation), citing the query line.
It names a test that requests another user's note id and expects a refusal.
It also notes the missing-note case returning undefined.

evals.name: streak-across-months
evals.prompt: Is the streak logic safe?
evals.expected_output: Finds that getDate() uses the day of the month in local time, so streaks break across month ends and time zones.
assertions: It reports the month-end break and the time-zone dependence (time and place).
It names a test with recordings on 31 October and 1 November.

evals.name: webhook-twice
evals.prompt: We just added billing webhooks. Anything risky?
evals.expected_output: Finds that a redelivered webhook inserts a second subscription and grants 100 credits again.
assertions: The webhook delivered twice (idempotency) is among the top three findings, citing the insert and the credits update.
It recommends an event id check or a unique constraint and a test that delivers the same event twice.

evals.name: missing-production-setting
evals.prompt: what could break when this goes to production?
evals.expected_output: Finds that missing keys are read without a check and that API_BASE silently falls back to localhost in production.
assertions: It reports the silent localhost fallback (the release itself) as high because nobody would notice.
It recommends checking required settings at start-up.

evals.name: main-path-untested
evals.prompt: edge cases for the share card please
evals.expected_output: Reports that no test exercises the share text at all, and that a score of exactly 70 reads as okay; few conditions apply.
assertions: It reports the untested main path as its own finding.
It lists most families as not applicable, each with a one-line reason.
It reports fewer than 10 findings.

evals.name: already-covered
evals.prompt: Check pay-submit-safe.ts for edge cases
evals.expected_output: Reports that pay-submit-safe-check.ts does not prove a single charge: it checks that the same key was sent and never counts charges, so a single charge depends on the server. Keeps the case as handled but untested, and also raises the unchecked error status.
assertions: Says the test does not prove one charge, because it checks the key and never counts charges.
Does not count the double charge as handled and tested.
Any remaining finding cites evidence.
